items.zh: 於自愆犯審諦了知，深見過失。既審了知深見過已，其未犯者，專意護持；其已犯者，於佛菩薩同法者所，至心發露如法悔除。
items.en: Regarding one's own failings and transgressions, one honestly recognises them, genuinely seeing their gravity. Having honestly recognised and genuinely seen this, whatever remains unbroken one guards with focused intent; whatever has already been broken, one sincerely confesses before the Buddha, before bodhisattvas, or before fellow practitioners, and repents in accordance with the teaching.

items.zh: 如是等類所有引攝、護持、增長諸善法戒，是名菩薩攝善法戒。
items.en: All such wholesome practices gathered, protected, and increased in this way are called a bodhisattva's discipline gathering wholesome practice.

items.title: Section: Discipline Benefiting Beings Opens — Eleven Aspects, and What Counts as Genuine Benefit

items.zh: 云何菩薩饒益有情戒？當知此戒略有十一相。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's discipline benefiting beings? This discipline should be understood as, in brief, eleven aspects.

items.zh: 何等十一？

items.title: Section: Being a Genuine Companion — In Worldly Tasks and in Illness

items.zh: 謂諸菩薩，於諸有情能引義利彼彼事業，與作助伴。於諸有情隨所生起疾病等苦瞻侍病等，亦作助伴。
items.en: Bodhisattvas become a genuine companion in whatever endeavour genuinely brings beings benefit. They likewise become a genuine companion in attending to any being suffering the pain of illness, tending to them accordingly.

items.title: Section: Teaching the Essential Dharma — Five Skilful Qualities, Three Principled Ones

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，依世出世種種義利，能為有情說諸法要；先方便說，先如理說，後令獲得彼彼義利。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, resting on every kind of worldly and transcendent benefit, are able to teach beings the essential dharma — first speaking accommodatingly and first speaking in accordance with genuine principle, and afterwards bringing the listener to attain that very benefit.

items.title: Remembering and Repaying Kindness, Rescuing From Fear, Resolving Grief

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，於先有恩諸有情所，善守知恩，隨其所應現前酬報。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, towards any being who has shown them kindness in the past, genuinely hold and recognise that kindness, repaying it directly in whatever manner actually fits.

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，於墮種種師子、虎狼、鬼魅、王賊、水火等畏諸有情類，皆能救護，令離如是諸怖畏處。又諸菩薩，於諸喪失財寶親屬諸有情類，善為開解，令離愁憂。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, towards beings caught in fear of lions, tigers, wolves, malevolent spirits, oppressive rulers or bandits, flood or fire, are able to rescue them, freeing them from these fearful circumstances. Bodhisattvas, towards beings who have lost wealth or family, skilfully help them find relief, freeing them from grief.

items.title: Section: Giving Life's Necessities — Except What Merely Feeds Indulgence

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，於有匱乏資生眾具諸有情類，施與一切資生眾具。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, towards beings genuinely lacking life's necessities, give every genuine necessity.

items.title: Section: Leading a Community Rightly — Teaching Each According to Their Own Vehicle

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，隨順道理，正與依止，如法御眾。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, in accordance with genuine principle, rightly provide support, leading their community according to the teaching.

items.title: Going Along With Worldly Customs — Except Where Genuine Harm Would Result

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，隨順世間事務言說，呼召去來，談論慶慰，隨時往赴，從他受取飲食等事。以要言之，遠離一切能引無義、違意現行，於所餘事心皆隨轉。
items.en: Bodhisattvas go along with ordinary worldly customs and speech — greetings and farewells, conversation, celebration and comfort, attending gatherings when the occasion calls, sharing food with others. Stated concisely: whatever would bring about something genuinely harmful or run against another's own wishes is set aside; in everything else, one simply goes along.

items.title: Revealing Genuine Virtue — Sometimes Openly, Sometimes Discreetly

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，若隱若露顯示所有真實功德，令諸有情歡喜進學。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, whether discreetly or openly, make known a being's genuine virtue, so that they take joy in continuing to practise.

items.title: Section: Correcting the Erring — Genuine Affection Beneath a Firm Method

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，於有過者，內懷親昵利益安樂增上意樂，調伏、訶責、治罰、驅擯；為欲令其出不善處，安置善處。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, towards one who has erred, hold inwardly a warm affection and an elevated wish for their benefit and peace, while outwardly taming them through reproach, discipline, or exclusion — precisely in order to bring them out of an unwholesome state and settle them in a wholesome one.

items.title: Section: Demonstrating Supernatural Power to Benefit Beings — Comprehensive Discipline Concludes

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，以神通力方便示現那落迦等諸趣等相，令諸有情厭離不善；方便引令入佛聖教，歡喜信樂，生希有心，勤修正行。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, through the skilful means of supernatural power, display the appearance of hell and the other lower realms, causing beings to turn away from wrongdoing in disgust; and, through skilful means, draw others into the Buddha's noble teaching, so that they feel genuine joy and faith, a sense of wonder, and diligently cultivate genuine practice.

items.title: Section: From Naming the Precepts to Actually Abiding in Them

items.zh: 云何菩薩住律儀戒，住攝善法戒，住饒益有情戒？善護律儀戒，善修攝善法戒，善行一切種饒益有情戒？
items.en: How does a bodhisattva abide in restraint discipline, abide in discipline gathering wholesome practice, and abide in discipline benefiting beings? How does one skilfully guard restraint discipline, skilfully cultivate discipline gathering wholesome practice, and skilfully practice discipline benefiting beings in its every kind?

items.title: Section: Abiding in Restraint Begins — Renouncing a Universal Monarch's Throne Like Discarding Garbage

items.zh: 謂諸菩薩，住別解脫律儀戒時，捨轉輪王而出家已，不顧王位，如棄草穢。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, abiding in individually liberating restraint discipline, having renounced a universal monarch's throne to become a monk, do not look back on that throne, discarding it as one discards rotting garbage.

items.zh: 如有貧庶為活命故，棄下劣欲而出家已，不顧劣欲，不如菩薩清淨意樂，捨輪王位而出家已，不顧一切人中最勝轉輪王位。
items.en: Just as someone genuinely poor, for the sake of mere survival, renounces base pleasures to become a monk and never looks back on them — a bodhisattva's own pure aspiration goes further still, renouncing even a universal monarch's throne, the very greatest position among all humankind, without the slightest backward glance.

items.title: Section: Not Hoping for Future Heavenly Pleasures, Not Clinging to Present Honour — Like Food Already Vomited

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，住律儀戒，於未來世天魔王宮所有妙欲，不生喜樂。亦不願求彼諸妙欲，修行梵行。於彼妙欲尚如實觀，猶如趣入廣大種種恐畏稠林，況餘諸欲。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, abiding in restraint discipline, take no delight even in the exquisite pleasures of a future palace of Śakra among the gods or of Māra. ... They genuinely observe even these pleasures as like entering a vast, dense forest full of terrifying dangers — how much more so, then, any lesser pleasure.

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，既出家已，於現在世尊貴有情種種上妙利養恭敬，正慧審觀尚如變吐曾不味著，何況於餘卑賤有情所有下劣利養恭敬。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, having renounced worldly life, examine with genuine wisdom even the finest support and honour offered by society's most exalted figures, and find it exactly like food already vomited, never again to be savoured — how much more so, then, the lesser honour offered by the humble.

items.title: Section: Delighting in Solitude, Never Resting Content With Restraint Alone

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，常樂遠離，若獨靜處，若在眾中，於一切時心專遠離寂靜而住。
items.en: Bodhisattvas constantly delight in solitude — whether alone in a quiet place or amid a crowd, at every moment the mind remains focused on genuine seclusion, abiding in stillness.

items.zh: 不唯於是尸羅律儀而生喜足，依戒、住戒，勤修無量菩薩等持，為欲引發證得自在。
items.en: They are not satisfied with restraint discipline alone; resting on and abiding in discipline, they diligently cultivate the boundless meditative states of a bodhisattva, in order to bring forth and realise genuine mastery.

items.title: Section: Clearing Away Improper Talk — How the Same Craving Can Be Redirected, Not Merely Suppressed

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，雖處雜眾，而不樂為乃至少分不正言論；居遠離處，不起少分諸惡尋思。或時失念暫爾現行，尋便發起猛利悔愧，深見其過。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, even amid a mixed crowd, take no delight in even the slightest improper talk; dwelling in seclusion, they do not give rise to even the slightest unwholesome thought. Should a lapse of mindfulness briefly occur, they immediately give rise to intense remorse and shame, genuinely seeing the fault in it.

items.zh: 數數悔愧，深見過故，雖復暫起不正言論、諸惡尋思，而能速疾安住正念，於彼獲得無復作心。由此因緣，則能拘檢。
習拘檢故，漸能如昔於彼現行深生喜樂，於今安住彼不現行喜樂亦爾。又能違逆，令不現起。
items.en: Through habituated self-restraint, one gradually comes to feel, towards abiding in the non-arising of affliction now, the very same depth of delight once felt indulging in its arising before — and is thereby able to actively counter it, preventing it from arising at all.

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，於諸菩薩一切學處，及聞已入大地菩薩廣大無量不可思議長時最極難行學處，心無驚懼，亦不怯劣。

blocks.text: The third storehouse, benefiting beings, then the beginning of a detailed account of how a bodhisattva actually lives in restraint.
"Whatever has been broken, one sincerely confesses before the Buddha, before bodhisattvas, or before fellow practitioners." Venerable Miào Jìng: not doing good is one fault; doing wrong is another.

Being a companion in their worthwhile tasks and in illness; teaching the Dharma "first in accommodating speech, then in accordance with principle"; remembering and repaying kindness; rescuing from fear ("lions, wolves, oppressive rulers, flood or fire"); resolving grief; giving necessities (except what feeds indulgence); leading a community rightly; going along with worldly customs (greetings, celebrations, sharing food) "except where real harm would result"; making others' virtue known; correcting those who err ("inwardly warm affection, outwardly firm method"; Venerable Miào Jìng: reproof, discipline, expulsion are mild, middle, severe); and using supernormal power to turn beings from wrong.

How does one live these precepts? A bodhisattva who has "renounced a universal monarch's throne to become a monk does not look back on it, discarding it as one discards grass". Master Cháng Bǎi explains the grades of wheel-turning kings.
"They take no delight even in the pleasures of Śakra's or Māra's palaces." Even the finest offerings from society's highest figures they see "exactly like food already vomited".

"Whether alone or amid a crowd, the mind remains focused on seclusion." If an unwholesome thought arises, one sees its fault, and "gradually comes to feel, towards the non-arising of affliction, the same depth of delight once felt in indulging it".

quiz.q: "Regarding one's own faults" — how do the lectures distinguish "qiān" from "fàn," and which kind of discipline is involved?
options: failing to do good one should is qiān; doing wrong is fàn; here it means violations of the discipline of gathering wholesome practice, not the seven assemblies' precepts
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: not doing meritorious deeds is qiān; doing wrongful deeds is fàn. Master Cháng Bǎi: here these refer specifically to violations of the discipline of gathering wholesome practice, not to the seven assemblies' precepts. The English "faults" merges the two.

quiz.q: For what has already been broken, before whom does the treatise say one sincerely confesses and repents?
options: before the Buddha, bodhisattvas, or fellow practitioners
quiz.why: "Whatever has already been broken, one sincerely confesses before the Buddha, before bodhisattvas, or before fellow practitioners." Master Cháng Bǎi: first before the Buddha, second before fellow bodhisattvas, third before fellow practitioners of the holy life.

quiz.q: When teaching beings the essential dharma, how does the treatise describe the sequence?
options: first speaking accommodatingly, first speaking according to principle, then leading them to attain that benefit
quiz.why: "Resting on every kind of worldly and transcendent benefit, [bodhisattvas] are able to teach beings the essential dharma." Master Cháng Bǎi: they teach without craving, not for fame, gain, or honour.

quiz.q: "Give every genuine necessity." Of the ten kinds of necessities, which does Master Cháng Bǎi say a bodhisattva does not give?
options: song, laughter, dance, and music, and sexual relations
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: of these ten kinds of necessities, apart from song, laughter, dance, and music, and sexual relations, the bodhisattva may give them all. Venerable Miào Jìng: the ninth, illumination, means lamps.

quiz.q: Bodhisattvas go along with worldly customs. What is the concise principle?
options: set aside whatever brings harm or goes against another's wishes; in everything else, go along
quiz.why: "Whatever would bring about something genuinely harmful or run against another's own wishes is set aside; in everything else, one simply goes along." Venerable Miào Jìng: happy occasions call for celebration; unhappy, inauspicious ones call for comfort.

quiz.q: Why do bodhisattvas reproach, discipline, or exclude one who has erred?
options: to bring them out of an unwholesome state and settle them in a wholesome one, holding inward affection and the wish for their benefit
quiz.why: Bodhisattvas hold "inwardly a warm affection and an elevated wish for their benefit and peace … precisely in order to bring them out of an unwholesome state and settle them in a wholesome one." Master Cháng Bǎi: inwardly they feel close to the person, as parents love their children.

quiz.q: Having renounced a universal monarch's throne to become a monk, how does the bodhisattva regard that throne?
options: does not look back, discarding it like grass and refuse
hands it to a son to control
quiz.why: "Having renounced a universal monarch's throne to become a monk, [they] do not look back on that throne, discarding it as one discards rotting garbage." Venerable Miào Jìng: regretting that monastic life is plain and thinking it better to be a monarch — he would never do that.
